headline: Menu crash fixes + song name retranslations
summary: Fixes the friend-menu / sing / hum / clothing-codec / bug-registering crashes by re-cooking how overlay strings get stored. Restores 15 NPC dialog bodies that were getting skipped because of a stray page-break. Retranslates 29 song titles where the AI had drifted from the Japanese (most visibly "Cottage Cheese" for what should have been "Summer Cottage").

shipFormats.label: Regular
shipFormats.description: Path A — overlay strings stored as plaintext, compressed flag flipped off. Larger on-disk, simpler bookkeeping.

shipFormats.label: Compressed overlay
shipFormats.description: Path B — overlay strings re-LZ-compressed with ndspy.codeCompression, on-disk shape closer to the original Konami layout.

shipNote: Both behave identically at runtime; pick by preference.

msgFileEdits.description: 15 dialog entries lost their body in v2.3 because the en_text gained a leading § (added during a canon sweep between v2.2 and v2.3). The reemit pipeline encoded that § as a 00 00 page-break, but the leading_cmds_hex for these entries already ends in 00 00, so the result was 00 00 00 00 back-to-back at the entry start. The renderer interpreted that as "end of page, next page is empty, skip to whatever's after" and fired the trailing [MENU:N] immediately. Body invisible, menu inescapable. Fixed by stripping exactly one leading § from these 15 rows. Detection was structural (en_text starts with § AND contains §[MENU:), so menu-choice-list entries where the leading § is correct were untouched.

songRetranslations.description: The original AI-generated translations for many song titles drifted significantly from the Japanese — most visibly entry 7 (なついろのコテージ, "Summer Cottage", which had been translated as "Cottage Cheese" and read as a food item in the in-game song menu). Reviewed all 96 entries; 29 corrected to track the JP meaning. Surviving entries unchanged. All replacements ≤ 20 characters (the slot budget).

overlayEdits.description: The ARM9 string pool and 6 UI overlays carry the menu / button / prompt text shown directly by the engine (not from message files). These slot widths are fixed: each new English string must fit within its original byte budget. See _patch_arm9_overlays.py for the production patcher.

compressedFlagFix.title: Compressed-flag flip (new in v2.31)
compressedFlagFix.description: In v2.3 every menu housed in one of these overlays (ov47, ov59, ov65, ov96, ov170, ov171) crashed the game or froze the player out. Root cause: the patcher wrote plaintext UTF-16 LE bytes into overlay file slots whose overlay-table entry still claimed compressed = True. The boot ROM would then try to LZ-decompress plaintext, get garbage, and the menu would either crash on open or freeze partway through. Fix (in _patch_arm9_overlays.py's apply_all): after each overlay's bytes are rewritten, also update the overlay-table u32 at +0x1C of the entry — clearing bit 24 (the compressed flag) and setting compressedSize to the new length. Two strategies offered via the OVERLAY_PATCH_MODE env var: MODE=A (write plaintext, clear flag, ships as the "regular" patch) and MODE=B (re-compress with ndspy.codeCompression.compress, keep flag set, update compressedSize to the new compressed length, ships as the "compressed overlay" patch).

groups.label: ARM9 string pool
groups.note: 26 strings at file offset 0xa6e44 (RAM 0x020a6e44). Pointer table at 0xa6ddc..0xa6e40 (26 u32 entries). All code references go through that pointer table, so in-place patching is safe as long as each new string fits in its original slot. Slot byte budget = (slot_bytes / 2) - 1 characters because each glyph is 2 bytes UTF-16 LE plus a 2-byte NUL terminator.

otherChanges.title: Two patch flavors shipped
otherChanges.body: v2.31 is the first release to ship two parallel patch flavors. The regular patch (Path A) stores patched overlay bytes as plaintext and flips the overlay-table compressed flag off. The compressed-overlay patch (Path B) re-LZ-compresses the patched bytes and keeps the flag set, which produces a smaller .nds file (~7 KB saved across the 6 patched overlays) and preserves the on-disk shape closer to the original Konami layout. Both behave identically at runtime.

otherChanges.title: Overlay patcher mode controlled by env var
otherChanges.body: _patch_arm9_overlays.py now reads OVERLAY_PATCH_MODE (default B). Mode A writes plaintext + clears the compressed flag; mode B re-compresses + keeps it. Mode B verifies the compress/decompress round-trip against the patched bytes before committing — any drift raises RuntimeError so a bad ndspy run can't silently corrupt an overlay.

otherChanges.title: Known issues — deferred
otherChanges.body: A wider sweep of leading-§ entries (865 rows with leading § + non-empty leading_cmds + no [MENU: token) was sampled and most turn out to be menu choice lists using [OP_0012:N] opcodes instead of [MENU:N], which are correct as-is. A small subset are dialog body without a trailing menu, which might render with an extra blank page before the body — not the same crash-on-open symptom as the 15 fixed entries, so deferred to a follow-up pass. Many other AI-generated song translations are stylistic interpretations rather than literal and were left alone unless they read as items (Cottage Cheese was the clear case).
